messages:
incidents-bot: Heads up — scheduled maintenance planned for us-west2 (zone drain) originally 2024-06-12 02:00-03:00 UTC. Posting here for coordination.

alex (oncall): i'm primary for this window. quick change request: customer-facing window needs to shift 30m earlier to 01:30-02:30 UTC. Reason: traffic pattern looks lighter then, reduces tail risk.

ryan (sre): +1 on moving earlier. also propose we do a staggered drain: canary 2 nodes, then 8 node batch, then remainder. minimizes request redistribution pain.

maria (customer-success): will notify impacted accounts. can you drop a short template i can paste into CS comms and the status page? want to include expected impact and rollback criteria.

alex (oncall): draft statuspage template below (please tweak):

"""
Component: Inference Serving (hosted-us-west2)
Status: Degraded (Scheduled Maintenance)
Scheduled start: 2024-06-12 01:30 UTC
Estimated end: 2024-06-12 02:30 UTC
Details: We will be performing a rolling drain of serving nodes in us-west2 to apply kernel and container runtime updates. Some requests routed to the zone may see slightly increased latency or transient 503s for < 2 minutes during individual node drains. We will route traffic away from draining nodes and monitor throughput.
Customer impact: Best-effort; minor latency spikes and very short request errors possible. No data loss expected.
If symptoms exceed 5% error rate for >5 minutes we will pause and rollback.
"""

jess (pm): tidy. add link to operational status page and a contact for urgent escalations (support@redwood.ai and oncall pager).

devops-bot: canary-drain-plan uploaded to /ops/maintenance/1718234567/canary-plan.md — checksum: a3f9c2.

alex (oncall): ops playbook (short):
1) mark canary nodes to cordon\2) drain one canary, validate metrics for 10m\3) if OK, drain second canary, validate 10m\4) proceed to batch drains (8 node batches)\5) if error spike >5% or latency P95 increases >200ms, stop and rollback.

commands to run:

```bash
# cordon and drain node (example)
kubectl cordon node-usw2-abc
kubectl drain node-usw2-abc --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```

alex (oncall): health checks we'll monitor (grafana dashboards):
- inference.token_latency.p95 (route: hosted-us-west2)
- inference.request_errors.rate (5m)
- node_cpu_utilization (per node)

ryan (sre): I'll watch the global routing table in case the fallback region starts absorbing too much traffic. If route shuffle > 20% we may want to throttle cross-region failover.

maria (customer-success): CS template for email/portal:

"""
Subject: Planned maintenance — brief impact to inference in us-west2 (Jun 12)
Hello,
We will perform planned infrastructure maintenance in our us-west2 region on Jun 12 between 01:30–02:30 UTC. During the window some requests served from that region may experience brief latency increases or very short errors (<2 minutes) while we perform rolling updates. There is no expected data loss.
What we’re doing: rolling node drains and runtime updates to improve stability and security.
If you have concerns or must avoid any downtime, please reply and we’ll provide options (reschedule/bypass region).
Thanks,
Redwood Inference Support (support@redwood.ai)
"""

alex (oncall): escalation mapping for the window:
- Sev3 (increased error rate <10%): primary oncall (alex) -> respond in 15m -> engage ryan if persists
- Sev2 (error rate >10% OR sustained latency >300ms P95): page eng-sre and exec oncall (ryan) -> rollback drains

incidents-bot: pager-test scheduled at 01:15 UTC. This is a non-disruptive test; will send a test alert to the oncall group.

jess (pm): customer comm ok from me assuming maria pushes the email. also please include the statuspage update time: we should post the page 30 minutes before start.

alex (oncall): timeline:
- 01:00 UTC: statuspage update (pre-maint notice)
- 01:15 UTC: pager test (non-disruptive)
- 01:30 UTC: start canary 1
- 01:40 UTC: validation window 10m
- 01:50 UTC: canary 2
- 02:00 UTC: batch drains start
- 02:30 UTC: finish target

maria (customer-success): i'll send the email at 01:05 UTC and post the portal banner at 01:00 UTC. tagging support leads to stand by.

ryan (sre): quick note on rollback: if we decide to stop and rollback, we will uncordon nodes and restart old runtime container on drained nodes via the deployment rollback job. Example commands:

```bash
# uncordon
kubectl uncordon node-usw2-abc
# trigger deployment rollback (helm)
helm rollback inference-serving 3 --namespace=redwood-serving
```

alex (oncall): ok all — i'll take the first 30m. ryan on standby for escalation. maria will own customer comms. devops-bot will run the canary plan. please ack when ready.

ryan (sre): ack. monitoring panels up.

maria (customer-success): ack — email queued.

devops-bot: starting preflight checks (image sigs, node health) — report: all clear. :white_check_mark:

alex (oncall): thanks team. i'll update this thread live during the window with status updates and final completion notice.

incidents-bot: Thread tagged as #maintenance; auto-reminder scheduled for 00:50 UTC.

alex (oncall): FINAL (post-maint): completed rolling drains. observed one ~90s spike of 503s during canary, rolled back that single node, re-ran canary after patch; overall error rate stayed <1.5% across window. updating statuspage to 'Operational' and sending completion note to customers now. :tada:

maria (customer-success): completion email sent to impacted list and posted on portal. customers with concerns routed to support.

ryan (sre): follow-up items: add a 5m delay between batches next run to reduce cascading rebalancing. filing infra ticket INF-472 to capture.

alex (oncall): handback: i'm handing back to night shift oncall @sam in 02:50 UTC. live metrics look stable. closing thread.
